summary.text: 用 means ‘use’ or ‘put into effect.’ One paleographic interpretation reads its ancient graph as a handled container and proposes that the graph was reused for ‘use’ because the words sounded alike. The container’s spoken name is unknown, so that sound match cannot be verified.

formation.text: The formation is disputed. One interpretation treats the whole graph as a pictograph of a container, with its body on the left and handle on the right. The received 說文 analysis parses it as 卜 plus 中. Other accounts relate 用 and 同 as graphic variants or a divided graph, or describe 用 as 同 with a handle added and 同 as phonetic. The evidence does not settle these competing analyses or establish an internal sound component.

components.text: The whole graph is interpreted as a handled bucket or container, with its body on the left and handle on the right. On this account, the graph was later reused for ‘put into effect/use’ because the words may have sounded alike; the container’s spoken name is unknown, so the match cannot be verified.

history.text: A form catalogue indexes oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, seal-script and 說文 forms, but its text does not describe individual strokes or establish a detailed sequence of graphic changes.

The container interpretation differs from the received 說文 parsing 從卜從中. Other accounts relate 用 and 同 as graphic variants or a divided graph; another describes 用 as 同 with a handle added and assigns 同 a sound role. These analyses remain unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The proposed borrowing from a container picture to ‘put into effect/use’ cannot be tested phonetically because the depicted object’s spoken name is unknown. 用’s own reconstructed readings do not establish that missing name or a sound match.

Oracle-bone examples attest 用 in contexts indicating whether a proposed action was carried out, but the first occurrence and relative chronology of this use and the proposed container sense are unsettled. A Qin-slip container or measure use read 桶 does not determine their order.

senses.text: 用/不用 is reported after divination statements to indicate whether a proposed action was carried out. This attested use does not establish the graph’s original meaning.
One Qin-slip context is read 桶, ‘container’ or ‘measure.’ It preserves a container-related use but does not establish the graph’s original meaning or when this use arose.

senses.gloss: preposition equivalent to 以; sequential or causal conjunction
senses.text: Bronze-inscription examples include prepositional and conjunctive uses alongside the verb ‘use.’ The examples do not establish their relative chronology or development.
用 has the current meaning ‘use’ or ‘employ.’ The evidence does not establish a complete path from the attested inscriptional uses to its present range.

limitations.text: Several uses are attested, but the evidence does not establish a semantic development linking them. The proposed borrowing from a container picture to ‘carry out/use’ lacks a verifiable sound match because the pictured object’s spoken name is unknown.

overview.text: 用 means ‘use’ or ‘put into effect.’ One interpretation says its ancient container picture was reused to write ‘use’ because the words were thought to sound alike. The container’s spoken name is unknown, so that proposed sound match cannot be checked.

components.text: The whole graph is interpreted as a handled container. The proposed borrowing for ‘use’ depends on a sound match, but the container’s spoken name is unknown, so the match cannot be verified.
